features.text: The patient had a right medial unicompartmental arthroplasty six weeks prior.
The patient experiences numbness on the side of her right knee, where the incision was.
The numbness has been present since immediately after the surgery and has not changed much.
The patient does not experience pain, tingling, or weakness in the affected area.
The patient is undergoing physical therapy to build strength and range of motion.
The numbness has not caused any difficulty with daily activities or physical therapy.
The patient has not undergone nerve conduction studies or EMG to evaluate the numbness.
The patient's surgeon mentioned that the numbness may improve as the nerves heal.
The patient has not noticed any changes in the numbness over the past few weeks.
The patient has not experienced any increased sensitivity, pain, or unusual sensations in the numb area.
The patient has not experienced any difficulty with movement or coordination in her right leg.
The patient has not had any numbness or tingling in other parts of her body.
The patient has not noticed any changes in her ability to move her right leg or foot.
The patient is focused on physical therapy and is being patient with the healing process.
